# SystemEntropy

The operating system's generator, as an [`EntropySource`](/docs/api/entropy/entropy-source).

```rux
pub struct SystemEntropy {}
```

Holds nothing: the system's generator needs no handle, no seed and no shutdown. It exists so that code taking a
source can be handed the real one.

## Constructors

<h3 id="new"><code>SystemEntropy</code></h3>

```rux
pub func SystemEntropy() -> SystemEntropy
```

The operating system's generator.
Takes nothing and cannot fail. Costs nothing to make, so there is no reason to keep one around rather than
making one where it is needed.
Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: the source, which holds no state of its own

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Entropy/Src/Fill.rux#L45)

## Implements EntropySource

`SystemEntropy` conforms to [`EntropySource`](/docs/api/entropy/entropy-source).

<h3 id="fill"><code>Fill</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Fill(self: &var SystemEntropy, buffer: *var opaque, length: uint) -> ! EntropyError
```

Fills `length` bytes of `buffer` from the operating system.
Exactly [`FillFromSource`](/docs/api/entropy/system-entropy#fill-from-source), reached through the interface. Succeeds only when every byte was written.
Runs in time proportional to `length` and allocates nothing.
`buffer` must be writable for `length` bytes.

| Name     | Type          | Description            |
| -------- | ------------- | ---------------------- |
| `buffer` | `*var opaque` | receives the bytes     |
| `length` | `uint`        | how many bytes to fill |

**Returns**: nothing when every byte was written, or why not

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Entropy/Src/Fill.rux#L60)

## Related

<h3 id="max-entropy-attempts"><code>MaxEntropyAttempts</code></h3>

```rux
pub const MaxEntropyAttempts: uint = 16;
```

How many times a fill will go back to an interrupted source before giving up.
A signal arriving during the call is ordinary and retrying is correct, but a process taking signals steadily
must not spin forever inside what its caller believes is one operation. Reaching this reports `Interrupted`,
which says exactly that and leaves trying again to the caller, who knows whether it is worth it.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Entropy/Src/Source.rux#L31)

<h3 id="max-entropy-request"><code>MaxEntropyRequest</code></h3>

```rux
pub const MaxEntropyRequest: uint = 0xFFFFFFFF;
```

The largest request the source accepts in a single call.
Windows takes a 32-bit count, so this is what a portable caller may ask for at once. A larger buffer is filled by
asking more than once, which `Fill` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Entropy/Src/Source.rux#L37)

<h3 id="fill-from-source"><code>FillFromSource</code></h3>

```rux
pub func FillFromSource(buffer: *var opaque, length: uint) -> ! EntropyError
```

Fills `length` bytes of `buffer` from the system's generator, in one pass.
`buffer` is borrowed and written; `length` is read by value. Succeeds only when every byte was written.
A zero length succeeds without touching anything. A length past what the source accepts is reported before the
buffer is looked at, so an impossible request is refused whatever was passed with it; a null buffer with an
ordinary length reports `Failed` rather than being written through.
On Linux and FreeBSD a short count is not a failure, so this loops until the buffer is full; a signal in the
middle is retried up to [`MaxEntropyAttempts`](/docs/api/entropy/system-entropy#max-entropy-attempts) times before reporting `Interrupted`. A kernel with no such call
reports `Unsupported`. On Darwin the source cannot fail. On Windows a request above [`MaxEntropyRequest`](/docs/api/entropy/system-entropy#max-entropy-request) reports
`TooLarge`, since the count is passed as 32 bits.
Runs in time proportional to `length` and allocates nothing.
`buffer` must be writable for `length` bytes. On any failure the buffer is zeroized, so a caller who ignores the
result gets zeros rather than a partly random buffer that would pass a glance.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Entropy/Src/Source.rux#L55)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type          | Description            |
| -------- | ------------- | ---------------------- |
| `buffer` | `*var opaque` | receives the bytes     |
| `length` | `uint`        | how many bytes to fill |

**Returns**: nothing when every byte was written in this one pass, or why not
